items.title: perf(mcp): skip HTTP preflight probe on reconnect
items.body:
## Problem

`MCPServerTask.run()` performs a content-type preflight probe (`_preflight_content_type`) before every HTTP MCP connection — including reconnects. For remote MCP servers (e.g. `beta.miaozhao.com/mcp`), this adds 1-3 seconds of redundant round trips on every reconnect cycle.

Observed with a remote waw MCP server:
```
15:34:58  reload.mcp received
15:35:00  job-posting (stdio) ready         ~0.7s
15:35:01  chrome (stdio) ready              ~1.0s
15:35:05  waw HTTP protocol negotiated      ~7s  (includes preflight HEAD 405 + GET 406)
15:35:10  waw list_tools completed           +5s
          Total: ~14s — exceeds waw-web BFF timeout of 13.7s
```

The preflight sends HEAD (returns 405) then GET (returns 406) — ~3s of network RTTs that provide no actionable information on reconnect since the URL was already validated on first connect.

## Fix

Skip preflight when `self._ready.is_set()` — the server has connected successfully before, so the URL is known-good.

```diff
-            if config.get("transport") != "sse":
+            if config.get("transport") != "sse" and not self._ready.is_set():
```

- **First connection**: preflight runs as before (URL validation preserved)
- **Reconnect**: preflight skipped, saves 1-3 RTTs per cycle

File: `tools/mcp_tool.py`, line ~1803 in `_run_http` call site within `run()`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent main branch (commit `c8e80cd0b`)
- Remote HTTP MCP server with RTT ~700ms (HEAD 405, GET 406)
- MCP keepalive triggers reconnect every ~3 minutes on connection drop

items.title: Dashboard TUI: Interface auto-refreshes and jumps even without new messages
items.body:
## Bug Description

In Dashboard TUI mode (`hermes dashboard --tui`), the interface **automatically refreshes and jumps/scrolls** at irregular intervals, even when:
- **No new messages are being generated**
- **No user input is occurring**
- **The agent is idle**

This makes it **extremely difficult to read historical messages**, as the view constantly jumps away from what the user is trying to read. The user has to repeatedly scroll back to the position they were reading, only for it to jump again seconds later.

## Severity

**High** — This significantly degrades the user experience to the point where the Dashboard TUI is practically unusable for reviewing conversation history. Users are forced to switch to CLI mode (`hermes --resume`) just to read past messages without interruption.

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS 26.4.1
- *+Hermes version**: Latest (installed via curl script)
- *+Browser**: Chrome/Safari (reproducible across browsers)
- *+Dashboard command**: `hermes dashboard --tui --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9120`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Dashboard TUI: `hermes dashboard --tui`
2. Open browser at `http://127.0.0.1:9119` (or configured port)
3. Have a conversation with some history (or restore a session with history)
4. Scroll up to read historical messages
5. Wait 5-30 seconds without doing anything
6. **Observe**: The view automatically jumps/scrolls without any new message or user action

## Expected Behavior

The interface should remain stable when:
- No new messages are being generated
- No user input is occurring
- The user is manually scrolling/reading history

Auto-scroll to bottom should only happen when:
- A new message is actively being generated AND
- The user is already at/near the bottom of the conversation

If the user has manually scrolled up to read history, auto-scroll should be **suspended** until the user explicitly returns to the bottom.

## Actual Behavior

The interface refreshes/jumps at irregular intervals (every few seconds to tens of seconds) even in complete idle state. This happens:
- Without any new message generation
- Without any WebSocket message that would justify a re-render
- While the user is actively reading historical content

## Additional Context

This issue is related to but distinct from other known Dashboard TUI bugs:
- **Mouse wheel stops working after resuming a session** (WebSocket connection issue)
- **Cannot view historical session list** (frontend fetch/rendering issue)

All three issues suggest **frontend React component state management and WebSocket handling** need significant stabilization.

## Current Workaround

Users must switch to CLI mode for reading history:
```bash
hermes sessions list
hermes --resume <session_id>
```

## Suggested Fix

1. **Debounce auto-scroll**: Only auto-scroll on actual new message events, not on arbitrary state updates or WebSocket heartbeats
2. **Detect user scroll position**: Track if user has manually scrolled away from bottom; if so, disable auto-scroll and show a "New messages" indicator instead
3. **Audit re-render triggers**: Review React state updates in the chat component to ensure idle state doesn't trigger unnecessary re-renders
4. **Separate heartbeat from UI updates**: WebSocket ping/pong should not trigger component re-renders

items.body:
## The Problem

When context compaction triggers during a Telegram conversation, the compacted messages are **visually removed from the user's chat view**. From the user's perspective, messages simply vanish — it looks like the agent deleted them.

This is extremely disruptive. The user loses their train of thought, can't scroll back to reference what was just discussed, and feels like the agent is erasing the conversation. Quoting the user: **"kills the train of thought"** and **"most disturbing."**

## What Happens

1. Long conversation builds up context
2. Context compaction fires (automatically, no user warning)
3. A large `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]` block replaces the actual messages in the chat
4. The user sees: their messages are gone, replaced by a wall of system text

## Why This Is a UX Emergency

- The user has **no warning** before messages disappear
- The user has **no control** over when it happens
- The compaction summary is injected as a visible assistant message (related: #38389)
- It often happens **mid-task**, destroying active context
- On messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord), the messages are gone from the chat history — the user can't scroll up to see them

## Expected Behavior

1. Compaction should be **invisible to the user** — it's an internal context management operation
2. The visible chat history should remain intact
3. If a summary must be shown, it should be a brief, non-intrusive system note, not a massive text block
4. Users should at minimum get a heads-up: "Context is full, summarizing earlier messages..."

## Related Issues

- #38389 — compaction summaries injected as visible messages

items.title: Windows gateway logging should tolerate Unicode in rotating log handlers
items.body:
# GitHub Issue Draft (English)

Title: Windows gateway logging should tolerate Unicode in rotating log handlers

## Summary

While operating a long-lived Hermes gateway on native Windows, the gateway became unresponsive during the pre-agent session hygiene path for a large Discord session. The failure was initially hard to classify because the gateway process stopped before the next diagnostic log line and before the agent turn started.

After adding narrow trace points, the stop was isolated to the existing session hygiene log message that contains Unicode punctuation:

```text
Session hygiene: ... — auto-compressing ...
```

A later direct log showed the concrete Windows encoding failure:

```text
UnicodeEncodeError: 'cp949' codec can't encode character '\u2014'
Message: 'Session hygiene: %s messages, ~%s tokens (%s) — auto-compressing ...'
```

I am not attaching raw logs because they include local session identifiers and workspace paths. The timeline below is sanitized.

## Environment

- OS: Windows, native PowerShell / Task Scheduler gateway run
- Gateway platform: Discord gateway with local HTTP API also enabled
- Session shape: long-lived Discord session, 400 stored messages at the hygiene check
- Model/provider in use: OpenAI Codex provider through OAuth
- Locale signal: the failing log sink attempted `cp949`

Note: this was observed in a Windows conversion fork. If current `main` already covers part of this through UTF-8 log handlers, this report may be useful as a release/backport/regression-test case rather than a new design request.

## Observed Sequence

The gateway repeatedly stopped in the same large-session path:

1. Inbound Discord message was received.
2. Existing session was resolved.
3. Transcript was loaded with 400 messages.
4. Session hygiene decided compression was needed.
5. A direct trace recorded `GW_HYGIENE_NOTICE_BEFORE`.
6. No `GW_HYGIENE_NOTICE_AFTER` appeared.
7. Gateway did not enter `_run_agent`.

After replacing the Unicode human-readable log with an ASCII-only trace locally, the same session passed the previous stop point, compressed the transcript, rewrote the session, and entered the agent conversation.

## Local Patch Tested

The durable local fix was to make Hermes rotating file handlers explicitly UTF-8 and tolerant of unencodable characters:

```python
handler = RotatingFileHandler(
    str(path),
    maxBytes=max_bytes,
    backupCount=backup_count,
    encoding="utf-8",
    errors="replace",
)
```

I also added a regression test that logs both an em dash and an arrow through `setup_logging()` and reads `agent.log` as UTF-8:

```text
Session hygiene: 400 messages, ~174,534 tokens — auto-compressing → done
```

## Verification

Local verification after the patch:

- `py_compile` passed for `hermes_logging.py` and the updated test file.
- Targeted pytest passed:
  - existing duplicate handler test
  - new Unicode rotating log handler test
- Gateway restarted successfully under the Windows scheduled task.
- `/health` returned `ok`.
- The original long-session gateway path no longer stopped at the Unicode session hygiene log point.

## Why This Matters

Gateway logs can contain Unicode from:

- session hygiene messages (`—`, `→`)
- status/progress symbols
- localized user messages
- tool output previews

On Windows systems where a log sink inherits a non-UTF-8 encoding, a logging call should not be able to interrupt or kill gateway progress. Even when the underlying model/provider has separate issues, the gateway should remain observable and recoverable.

## Suggested Fix

Please consider ensuring every gateway/agent rotating file log handler is opened with:

```python
encoding="utf-8",
errors="replace",
```

and adding a regression test that writes Unicode punctuation through the real logging setup.

## Summary

When running `hermes update`, the update process correctly detects a running dashboard whose backend no longer matches the updated frontend and stops the process. However, it has no awareness of whether the dashboard is managed by systemd (user or system service). It always prints the generic manual command `hermes dashboard --port <port>` instead of suggesting the appropriate `systemctl --user restart` (or `systemctl restart`) command.

In the reported case, the user-level service (`hermes-dashboard.service`) had a restart policy and automatically brought the dashboard back up, so there was no actual downtime. The issue is purely one of poor messaging and lack of integration with managed services.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up `hermes-dashboard.service` as a **user service** (`~/.config/systemd/user/`) with a restart policy because Hermes Desktop requires the dashboard backend.
2. Run `hermes update`.
3. The update stops the dashboard process and prints the generic manual restart command.
4. (In this case the service recovered automatically; in other configurations it may not.)

## Expected Behavior

After stopping a dashboard process due to a version mismatch, the update script should:

- Detect whether the process is managed by a systemd service (user or system).
- Print the correct restart command (`systemctl --user restart hermes-dashboard.service` or equivalent).
- Optionally acknowledge that a managed service was detected.

## Actual Behavior

The update always emits the same manual CLI instruction regardless of how the dashboard is being supervised. No attempt is made to discover or suggest the managed-service restart path.

## Environment

- Hermes version: post-2026-06-06 update
- OS: WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows
- Hermes Desktop connected to WSL backend
- Dashboard running as user-level systemd service (`hermes-dashboard.service`)
- Service automatically restarted after the update killed the old process

## Additional Context

- The service was intentionally created on 2026-06-05 to support Hermes Desktop.
- The backend/frontend mismatch protection logic is correct and desirable.
- The remaining gap is that the update process does not integrate with systemd-managed services when giving post-stop guidance.

## Suggested Fix

In the update logic, after stopping a dashboard process:

1. Check for the existence of a corresponding systemd unit (both system and user scopes).
2. If found, emit the appropriate `systemctl --user restart ...` (or `systemctl restart ...`) command instead of (or in addition to) the generic `hermes dashboard` command.
3. Consider making the message context-aware based on how the dashboard was originally launched.

## References

- Service file: `/home/don/.config/systemd/user/hermes-dashboard.service`

**Severity:** Low–Medium (Usability / Messaging)

### Bug Description

The Windows Native guide (`website/docs/user-guide/windows-native.md`) states at line 223-228 that the installer adds `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin` to User PATH and that `Get-Command hermes` should print `bin\hermes.cmd`.

However, the actual installer (`scripts/install.ps1`, lines 1567-1583) adds `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts` to User PATH instead:

```powershell
$hermesBin = "$InstallDir\venv\Scripts"
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "$hermesBin;$currentPath", "User")
```

There is no `hermes.cmd` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\` — that directory only contains `uv.exe`, `uvw.exe`, `uvx.exe`. The actual hermes command resolves to `venv\Scripts\hermes.exe` (the console-script entry point defined in `pyproject.toml`).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes on Windows using `install.ps1`
2. Open a new PowerShell session
3. Run `Get-Command hermes`
4. Compare the output path with what the documentation states

### Expected Behavior

The documentation (`windows-native.md`, lines 223-228) states:
- Installer adds `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin` to User PATH
- `Get-Command hermes` prints `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\hermes\bin\hermes.cmd`

### Actual Behavior

`Get-Command hermes` actually resolves to `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe`.
The directory `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\` contains only `uv.exe`, `uvw.exe`, `uvx.exe` — no `hermes.cmd` exists there.

Setup / Installation

The doc path `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin` was never added to PATH by the installer. The installer (`scripts/install.ps1`, lines 1567-1583) only ever adds `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts` to User PATH.

## Bug Description

When the Hermes Dashboard (`:9119`) is configured with `basic_auth` (username/password), the chat page shows a JavaScript console error:

```
Session token unavailable. Set HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN or use --token.
```

This occurs because the SPA checks for `window.__HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN__` at mount time without accounting for auth mode. When basic auth is enabled, the session token is irrelevant — authentication is cookie-based and the WebSocket connects via `/api/auth/ws-ticket`.

## Root Cause

In the chat page template (likely `dashboard/templates/chat.html` or similar), there's a check:

```javascript
!window.__HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN__ ? "Session token unavailable..." : null
```

This check runs unconditionally, even when `basic_auth` is enabled and `window.__HERMES_AUTH_REQUIRED__` is `true`.

## Reproduction Steps

   ```yaml
   dashboard:
     basic_auth:

         trojy: panatha13
   ```
2. Start dashboard: `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --skip-build`
3. Navigate to `http://localhost:9119/chat`
4. Log in with username/password
5. Check browser console → see "Session token unavailable" error

## Expected Behavior

When using basic auth, the session token check should be skipped since authentication is handled via cookies + ws-ticket.

## Proposed Fix

Change the condition to also check for auth mode:

```javascript
!window.__HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN__ && !window.__HERMES_AUTH_REQUIRED__
  ? "Session token unavailable. Set HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN or use --token."
  : null
```

Alternatively, guard the check in the server-side template so it's only rendered when auth is not enabled.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.15.1 (commit 56236b1)

items.title: [Bug]: CLI input locks up unrecoverably on lazy-dep install prompt (lazy_deps.py uses bare input() under prompt_toolkit)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Description

In CLI mode, the interactive prompt locks up the terminal completely whenever
Hermes's lazy dependency installer fires. Observed via `vision_analyze` on a
fresh install where Pillow was not present. The CLI becomes fully unresponsive:
no keyboard input is accepted, Ctrl-C does nothing, and the quit commands do not
work. Recovery requires killing the process from another terminal. Reproduces
every time.

The on-screen state when wedged:

```
Feature 'tool.vision' requires: Pillow==12.2.0
Install into the active venv now? [Y/n]
```

## Root cause (confirmed from source)

This is NOT pip prompting. It is Hermes's own lazy-install confirmation in
`tools/lazy_deps.py`. The prompt is emitted with a bare builtin `input()`:

```python
# tools/lazy_deps.py  (around lines 459-465)
if prompt and sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty():
    spec_list = ", ".join(missing)
    try:
        answer = input(
            f"\nFeature {feature!r} requires: {spec_list}\n"
            f"Install into the active venv now? [Y/n] "
        ).strip().lower()
    except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
        answer = "n"
```

In CLI mode `sys.stdin` and `sys.stdout` ARE TTYs, so the `isatty()` guard
passes and the branch runs. But the interactive CLI runs prompt_toolkit, which
owns stdin. A raw blocking `input()` competes with prompt_toolkit's event loop
for the same stdin: keystrokes are consumed by prompt_toolkit, the `input()`
call never receives the answer, and the whole session wedges with no way to
answer, interrupt, or quit.

This is the same failure mode as the closed confirmation-prompt hangs
**#23694 / #24343** (daemon-thread `input()` vs prompt_toolkit stdin). Those
fixes covered Hermes slash-command prompts; the `lazy_deps.py` prompt is a
separate code path that was not covered, so it still hangs.

The `isatty()` check is the wrong gate. It detects "attached to a terminal" but
not "another reader (prompt_toolkit) already owns stdin." Any lazy-install
trigger in an interactive CLI session hits this (vision/Pillow is just the
common one).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install where a lazy feature dependency is missing (e.g. Pillow absent,
   so `tool.vision` is unsatisfied).
2. Launch `hermes` in interactive CLI mode.
3. Trigger the feature (call `vision_analyze` on any image).
4. Hermes prints `Install into the active venv now? [Y/n]` and blocks on
   `input()`. The CLI accepts no input: cannot answer, cannot Ctrl-C, cannot
   quit. Recover only by killing the process from another terminal.

## Expected

When running under the interactive CLI, the confirmation must be routed through
prompt_toolkit (the same mechanism the slash-command confirmation fix uses)
rather than a bare `input()`, OR the prompt should be suppressed in favor of the
`security.allow_lazy_installs` config gate when prompt_toolkit owns stdin. The
session must stay answerable, interruptible, and quittable.

## Actual

Bare `input()` blocks under prompt_toolkit and never receives the keystroke.
Total input lockup; external kill is the only recovery. Reproduces every time.

## Workaround

Pre-install the dependency so the lazy path never triggers, e.g.
`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m pip install "Pillow==12.2.0"`.
(My earlier `pip install --no-input` suggestion does NOT help, because pip is
not the thing prompting; Hermes is.)

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)
- macOS 26.5.1 (build 25F80), Apple Silicon
- Python 3.11.15 (Hermes runtime)

## Related

- #23694 / #24343 — closed confirmation-prompt hangs, same `input()` vs
  prompt_toolkit stdin race. Those fixed slash-command prompts; `lazy_deps.py`
  is an uncovered sibling path.
- #33271 — terminal unresponsive after interrupting a running agent. Sibling
  input-lockup symptom, different trigger.
- #22111 — gateway terminal hangs on a blocking command. Same "foreground
  blocks the loop" class, different surface.
